SUSAN McSWEENEY  BRAD HALPERN  RAY PEARL  NED E DAVIS  KELLY HONIG

  Regular Meeting of the City Council

  .

  ATTEND OR WATCH THE MEETING
  Members of the public may attend in-person in the Council Chambers or watch the meeting
  through Zoom, City Website (Live Stream) or Cable TV Channel 10. City Council Chamber doors
  open 30 minutes before the meeting start time.

  PUBLIC COMMENT/SPEAKERS
  Members of the public may express comments to the City Council in person at the meeting or
  may submit written comments before or at the meeting. Submit a Public Speaker card or Written
  Comment card to the City Clerk prior to the public comment portion of that item. Public speakers
  are limited to three minutes unless the presiding officer sets a different limit for meeting
  management purposes. An oral summary of written comments may be given at the discretion of
  the presiding officer.

  Written comments may be emailed to the City Clerk's Office at cityclerk@wlv.org no later than
  4:00 p.m. on the meeting date. Written comments will be provided to City Council prior to the
  meeting and posted at https://www.wlv.org/569/City-Council-Supplemental-Packets

SUSAN McSWEENEY  BRAD HALPERN  RAY PEARL  NEDEDAVIS  KELLY HONIG
  Mayor  Mayor Pro Tern  Councilmember  Council member  Councilmember

  REGULAR MEETING MINUTES
  April 22, 2026
  CALL TO ORDER:

  This regular meeting of the Westlake Village City Council was called to order by Mayor
  Mcsweeney on Wednesday, April 22, 2026 at 6:34 p.m., at 31200 Oak Crest Drive,
  Westlake Village.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

  Mayor Mcsweeney invited Olivia Corbett, White Oak 4th Grade Student Mayor Delegate
  to lead the Pledge of Allegiance.

  ROLL CALL:

  PRESENT:  Councilmembers Honig, Davis, Pearl, Mayor Pro Tern Halpern, and
  Mayor Mcsweeney

  ABSENT:  None

  ROLL CALL FOR WHITE OAK ELEMENTARY SCHOOL STUDENTS:

  PRESENT:  Councilmembers Connor Petty, Avery Pepper, Sawyer Basis, Mayor
  Pro Tern Harper Sandefur, Mayor Olivia Corbett, and City Manager
  Emilia White

  ABSENT:  None

  Also Present:  City Manager de Geus, City Attorney Boga, Assistant City Manager
  Wilson, City Clerk Mann, Planning Director Asp, City Engineer
  Hughes, Assistant to the City Manager Mott, Administrative Analyst
  Hamilton, Community Services Manager Roush, Community
  Services Specialist Mattappally, Deputy City Clerk Kramer, and
  Planning Intern Anya Kargodorian.
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  April 22. 2026  2

APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

Councilmember Honig moved to approve the Agenda as presented. Councilmember
Pearl seconded the motion.

  YES:  Councilmembers Honig, Davis, Pearl, Mayor Pro Tern Halpern, and
  Mayor Mcsweeney
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

Mayor Mcsweeney declared the motion passed 5-0.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES:
Mayor Pro Tern Halpern moved to approve the Minutes of March 25, 2026 City Council
Regular Meeting. Councilmember Davis seconded the motion.

  YES:  Councilmembers Honig, Davis, Pearl, Mayor Pro Tern Halpern, and
  Mayor Mcsweeney
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

Mayor Mcsweeney declared the motion passed 5-0.

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS/CEREMONIAL MATTERS:

1.  City to Schools Program - White Oak Elementary School 4th Grade Students
  - Student Councilmembers and City Manager

  Mayor Mcsweeney discussed the education outreach program, City to Schools,
  and explained how White Oak 4th graders learn about civics and local government.
  Councilmembers thanked the students for their participation and assisting City
  Council.

2.  Proclamation Presentation - AYSO Region 4 - 50th Anniversary

  Mayor Mcsweeney recognized A YSO Region 4 in celebration of its 50th
  anniversary. Councilmember Pearl, together with fellow Councilmembers, shared
  personal family experiences with A YSO and expressed heartfelt appreciation to
  the volunteers, coaches, referees, and families for their many hours of dedication
  and commitment to youth sports, and for the positive impact they continue to have
  in our community.

  AYSO Commissioner Bill Barbato, addressed the City Council and thanked the
  City for its ongoing support and for the opportunity to celebrate this milestone.
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  April 22, 2026  3

PUBLIC COMMENTS: None

STAFF COMMENTS:

City Manager de Geus provided updates on the Berniece Bennett Park Playground
renovation, noting the project remains on schedule with reopening anticipated in early
May. Mr. de Geus reported the commencement of the Thousand Oaks Boulevard median
transformation project and reviewed anticipated timelines for upcoming Pure Water
Project roadway improvements. Earth Month activities, the Leaf Blower Rebate Program,
and "Stay Alert Don't Get Hurt" campaign were highlighted.

City Manager de Geus highlighted agenda topics for the upcoming Council Committee
meetings and City Council meetings.

COUNCIL COMMENTS:

Mayor Pro Tern Halpern promoted the Leaf Blower Rebate Program and noted this
meeting with the fourth-grade student council members is his favorite meeting of the year.

Councilmember Davis acknowledged Mayor McSweeney's leadership in championing the
Community Park.

Councilmember Pearl recognized the benefits of the Community Park, City to Schools
Program, AYSO, and thanked White Oak teachers Ms. Borg and Ms. Riveto.

MONTHLY DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS:

1.  Sheriff's Department Report

  Deputy Chad Ray presented the Sheriff's Department report for March 2026,
  outlining crime statistics for the month. He announced that the Lost Hills Sheriff's
  Station Open House will take place on May 2, 2026, from 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m.,
  and invited residents to attend.

  White Oak Student Councilmembers asked questions of Deputy Ray about his job.

2.  Fire Department Report

  Assistant Fire Chief Drew Smith presented the Fire Department's report for March
  2026, highlighting the total number of fire incidents, medical response calls, and
  rescue operations completed during the month. He announced that Fire Service
  Day is scheduled for May 9, 2026, from 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. at Station 89, located
  at 29575 Canwood Drive in Agoura Hills, and noted that Westlake Village's Station
  144 will participate in the event.

  White Oak Student Councilmembers asked questions of Assistant Fire Chief Smith
  about his job.
   --  ----  -----------------------

  City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  April 22, 2026  4

MONTHLY DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS (continued):

3.  Library Report

  Julie Frieze, Manager, Westlake Village Daniel K. Ludwig Library, presented the
  library's report for the month of March 2026 covering traffic, circulation, programs,
  and reference requests.

  White Oak Student Councilmembers asked questions of Library Manager Frieze
  about her job.

CITY COUNCIL COMMITTEE REPORTS: None

RECESS:

Mayor Mcsweeney and Student Mayor Olivia Corbett announced a short recess and
invited everyone to the courtyard for cupcakes and lemonade and thanked the White Oak
Elementary Students for their participation.

City Council recessed at 7:39 p.m.

RECONVENED:

City Council reconvened the Regular Meeting, at 7:55 p.m. with all City Councilmembers
in attendance.

PUBLIC HEARINGS:

1.  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 26-001; RESOLUTION NO. 2447-26

  Planning Intern Kargodorian presented a request for approval of Conditional Use
  Permit No. 26-001 for the off-site sale of beer and wine at a proposed takeout and
  catering kitchen located at 4619 Lakeview Canyon Road . Ms. Kargodorian
  described the proposed operation, including onsite preparation of focaccia bread
  and other food items, limited hours of operation, and use of existing shared
  parking. She noted the request is consistent with zoning and the General Plan and
  exempt from CEQA

  On April 1, 2026, the Land Use Committee (Pearl/Halpern) reviewed the proposal
  and recommended that the request move forward to a public hearing.

  Applicant Kyle Lopez addressed the City Council.
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  April 22, 2026  5

PUBLIC HEARINGS (continued):

  Councilmember Honig moved that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2447-26,
  determining Conditional Use Permit No. 26-001 is exempt from CEQA and
  authorizing the sale of beer and wine for off-site consumption at a takeout and
  catering kitchen located at 4619 Lakeview Canyon Road (La Gita Kitchen and
  Focacceria). Councilmember Pearl seconded the motion.

  YES:  Councilmembers Honig, Davis, Pearl, Mayor Pro Tern
  Halpern, and Mayor Mcsweeney
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

Mayor Mcsweeney declared the motion passed 5-0.

  RESOLUTION NO. 2447-26: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE APPROVING CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 26-001 TO
  AUTHORIZE THE SALE OF BEER AND WINE FOR OFF-SITE CONSUMPTION IN
  CONJUNCTION WITH A TAKEOUT AND CATERING RESTAURANT LOCATED AT
  4619 LAKEVIEW CANYON ROAD (LA GITA KITCHEN AND FOCACCERIA)

2.  FISCAL YEAR 2026-2027 ASSESSMENTS FOR LIGHTING AND LANDSCAPE
  ASSESSMENT DISTRICTS: RESOLUTION NOS. 2448-26, 2449-26 AND 2450-
  26

  City Engineer Hughes presented a request for consideration to levy Fiscal Year
  2026-27 assessments for Lighting Maintenance District No. 1, Landscape
  Maintenance District No. 1, and Westlake Spectrum Landscape District No. 15.
  She reviewed the annual assessment process required under the Landscaping
  and Lighting Act of 1972 and noted that no changes were proposed to existing
  assessment rates for any district. Ms. Hughes summarized proposed budgets,
  General Fund contributions, and projected fund balances, and outlined ongoing
  cost pressures affecting long-term financial sustainability.

  Mayor Pro Tern Halpern moved that City Council adopt Resolution Numbers 2448-
  26, 2449-26 and 2450-26 to Levy the Assessments for Fiscal Year 2026-27 within
  the Lighting Maintenance District No. 1, Landscape Maintenance District No. 1 and
  Westlake Spectrum Landscape District No. 15, direct the City Clerk and City
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  April 22, 2026  6

PUBLIC HEARINGS (continued):

  Engineer to file a certified copy of the Resolutions, Annual Assessments and
  Diagrams with the Los Angeles County Auditor-Controller. Councilmember Davis
  seconded the motion.

  YES:  Councilmembers Honig, Davis, Pearl, Mayor Pro Tern
  Halpern, and Mayor Mcsweeney
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

Mayor Mcsweeney declared the motion passed 5-0.

  RESOLUTION NO. 2448-26: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE CONFIRMING A DIAGRAM AND ASSESSMENT FOR THE
  2026-27 FISCAL YEAR, AND ORDERING THE IMPROVEMENTS IN CONNECTION
  WITH CITY OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE LIGHTING MAINTENANCE ASSESSMENT
  DISTRICT NO. 1 PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF PART 2 OF DIVISION 15 OF
  THE STREETS AND HIGHWAYS CODE

  RESOLUTION NO. 2449-26: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE CONFIRMING A DIAGRAM AND ASSESSMENT FOR THE
  2026-27 FISCAL YEAR, AND ORDERING THE IMPROVEMENTS IN CONNECTION
  WITH WESTLAKE VILLAGE LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE ASSESSMENT
  DISTRICT NO. 1 PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF PART 2 OF DIVISION 15 OF
  THE STREETS AND HIGHWAYS CODE

  RESOLUTION NO. 2450-26: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE CONFIRMING A DIAGRAM AND ASSESSMENT FOR THE
  2026-27 FISCAL YEAR, AND ORDERING THE IMPROVEMENTS IN CONNECTION
  WITH WESTLAKE SPECTRUM LOCAL LANDSCAPE ASSESSMENT DISTRICT NO.
  15 PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF PART 2 OF DIVISION 15 OF THE
  STREETS AND HIGHWAYS CODE

MONTHLY IN-HOUSE DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS:

1.  Engineering Department Report

  City Engineer Hughes presented the Engineering Report highlighting Community
  Park improvements, the Berniece Bennett Park playground equipment project with
  reopening scheduled for early May, early May roadwork under the Street
  Improvement Program, and the status of the Civic Center roof replacement project.
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  April 22, 2026  7

MONTHLY IN-HOUSE DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS (continued):

2.  Planning Department Report

  Planning Director Asp presented the Planning Department Report, highlighting the
  April 18, 2026 Shred Event, the Bob Theobald internship program, an Associate
  Planner recruitment update, adoption of the California Building and Fire Codes,
  modifications to the Accessory Dwelling Unit Ordinance, slope development
  standards, and an inventory of non-conforming walls.

3.  Cultural Recreation Report

  Community Services Manager Roush provided an update on recent and upcoming
  programs. For the City to Schools program, a mock City Council field trip was held
  on April 15, and the Student City Council members are participating tonight. The
  Earth Day Festival is planned for April 25 at Westlake Village Community Park and
  will include partner booths, activities, and community engagement. A trail clean-up
  at Wishbone Trail was rescheduled for May 2 and will be led by COSCA rangers,
  with registration required.

CONSENT CALENDAR:

Mayor Pro Tern Halpern moved to approve the Consent Calendar. Councilmember Pearl
seconded the motion.

  YES:  Councilmembers Honig, Davis, Pearl, Mayor Pro Tern
  Halpern, and Mayor Mcsweeney
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

Mayor Mcsweeney declared the motion passed 5-0.

  APPROVAL OF WARRANTS: Warrants effective April 15, 2026, in the amount
  of $672,527.45 (Warrant Register is on file with the City Clerk)

OLD BUSINESS:

1.  CLEAN POWER ALLIANCE OF SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA ELECTRIC FLEET
  TRANSITION PROGRAM - AUTHORIZATION TO INSTALL CHARGING
  STATIONS AT CIVIC CENTER AND PURCHASE ELECTRIC VEHICLE

  Administrative Analyst Hamilton presented a request for authorization to proceed
  with improvements under the Clean Power Alliance Electric Fleet Transition
  Program. He provided an update on the City's participation in the grant program,
  including prior approval of a Ford F-150 Lightning truck and remaining grant funds.
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  April 22. 2026  8

OLD BUSINESS (continued):

  Due to cost constraints, staff recommended a reduced scope consisting of the
  purchase of a Ford Mustang Mach-E for City use and the replacement of existing
  charging stations and installation of additional charging stations at the Civic
  Center. Mr. Hamilton noted that all costs would be reimbursed through grant
  funding and that the proposed actions support sustainability and fleet operations.

  City Council discussion addressed charging station limitations and responsibility
  for payment of charging costs.

  Councilmember Davis moved that the City Council authorize the City Manager to
  negotiate and execute agreements within the Council approved budget of
  $143,404 to replace the existing charging stations and install two additional
  charging stations at the Civic Center and $45,000 to purchase a new 2026 Ford
  Mach-E as part of the Clean Power Alliance Electric Fleet Transition Program
  Agreement. Mayor Pro Tern Halpern seconded the motion.

  YES:  Councilmembers Honig, Davis, Pearl, Mayor Pro Tern
  Halpern, and Mayor Mcsweeney
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

Mayor Mcsweeney declared the motion passed 5-0.

NEW BUSINESS:

1.  REVIEW OF THE COMPENSATION STUDY FINDINGS AND APPROVAL OF
  RELATED SALARY RANGE ADJUSTMENTS

  City Manager de Geus introduced the item and provided background on the City's
  comprehensive classification and compensation study, which is conducted by an
  outside consultant every four years. Matt Weatherly, President of Public Sector
  Personnel Consultants, presented the findings.

  Mr. Weatherly summarized the study methodology, which included a review of job
  classifications, salary ranges, and total compensation compared with comparable
  cities. He reported that the City's benefits were found to be competitive. The study
  recommended adjusting salary ranges to achieve a narrower, market-consistent
  spread and implementing select market adjustments to certain classifications to
  align salaries with median market levels, effective July 1, 2026.
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  April 22, 2026  9

NEW BUSINESS (continued):

  On April 3, 2026, the Administrative Committee (Mcsweeney/Halpern) reviewed
  the study and unanimously supported the recommendations. The City Council
  considered approval of the compensation study recommendations for inclusion in
  the Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget.

  City Council discussion included clarification of the proposed minimum, midpoint,
  and maximum monthly salary ranges and the associated salary differentials. The
  Council noted that this structure provides the City Manager with the flexibility and
  tools necessary to attract and retain high-quality staff.

  Mayor Pro Tern Halpern moved that the City Council approve the Compensation
  Study recommendations to be included in the Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget,
  including adjusting salary ranges to the 40% spread consistent with market trends.
  Councilmember Pearl seconded the motion.

  YES:  Councilmembers Honig, Davis, Pearl, Mayor Pro Tern
  Halpern, and Mayor Mcsweeney
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

Mayor Mcsweeney declared the motion passed 5-0.

2.  APPROVAL OF A THREE-YEAR AGREEMENT WITH VASQUEZ AND
  COMPANY LLP FOR AUDITING SERVICES

  Assistant City Manager Wilson presented a request for approval of a three-year
  professional services agreement with Vasquez and Company, LLP to provide
  independent auditing services beginning with Fiscal Year 2025-26. She reviewed
  the City's legal requirement for an annual audit, summarized the competitive
  request for proposals process, and recommended selection of Vasquez and
  Company based on qualifications, experience, and proposal evaluation. Ms.
  Wilson noted that engaging in a new firm ensures compliance with state audit
  partner rotation requirements and that sufficient funding is included in the City's
  budget.

  Ms. Wilson introduced Vasquez and Company's team including Cristy Canieda,
  Partner and Government Practice Leader, Roger Martinez, Partner and Audit
  Practice Leader, and Rhoda Dollaga, Audit Senior Manager. Mr. Martinez
  addressed the City Council providing a presentation of Vasquez and Company and
  the services they will be providing to the City. He described their audit approach
  focused on understanding City operations, evaluating internal controls, and
   ---- -  -  --------- -----

  City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  April 22, 2026  10

NEW BUSINESS (continued):

  reviewing information technology systems to support a thorough and effective
  audit. The firm emphasized its ability to meet required timelines and deliver
  high-quality audit services aligned with the City's needs.

  On April 13, 2026, the Administrative Committee (Mcsweeney/Halpern) received
  a presentation from the Vasquez team and had the opportunity to ask questions
  regarding their engagement. The Committee recommended that the agreement
  be moved to the full City Council for approval.

  City Council discussion included the clarification of the scope of the information
  technology (IT) component, explaining that IT general controls and key financial
  systems would be reviewed as part of the audit to support internal control
  assessment and audit reliability.

  Councilmember Davis moved that the City Council approve a three-year
  agreement with Vasquez and Company, LLP incorporating the rates and charges
  contained in the firm's cost proposal and authorizing the Mayor to execute the
  contract on behalf of the City. Councilmember Honig seconded the motion.

  YES:  Councilmembers Honig, Davis, Pearl, Mayor Pro Tern
  Halpern, and Mayor Mcsweeney
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

Mayor Mcsweeney declared the motion passed 5-0.

ADJOURNMENT:

Mayor Mcsweeney adjourned the meeting at 9: 18 p.m.
